draft.intro: Soccer is the busiest corner of this site by a distance, and the one that gets rebuilt most often, mostly because it is the one people keep coming back to. More than thirty games sit under this page, and they fall into two moods: quick guessing puzzles you can finish waiting for a bus, and long simulations where you sign players, answer to a board and eventually get sacked. All of it is free and plays in the browser without an account.
draft.whyHere: The split that matters here is how long you want to sit down for. Footle, Career Quiz and Missing XI are one answer puzzles: a stat line, a career history, a famous lineup with a gap in it. Soccer Grid, Connections and Transfer Path make you hold two things at once, a club and a season, or two players and the ground they once shared. Then the money games, which in soccer means fees and auctions rather than draft picks: $1B Budget Builder hands you a billion and eleven slots, Sign the Player drops you into a blind auction against two rivals, Player Stock Market buys you in at real past valuations and then runs a real year at you. And Soccer Career, Club Manager and Stadium Tycoon are not puzzles at all, they are evenings.

startHere.label: Career Ladder
startHere.why: The gentlest way into the guess the player games. You get his clubs one at a time in order, so you can reason your way there instead of staring at a stat line. Pick Who Am I? instead if you would rather be told how warm you are, and Footle if numbers are how your brain works.

startHere.label: Club Manager
startHere.why: The full management job, 330 real clubs across 20 leagues, today or in a real past season. Rebuild Challenge scratches the same itch in a fraction of the time, one club in trouble and a set of cuts you have to commit to. Soccer Career is the other side of the touchline, where you are the player rather than the boss.

startHere.label: $1B Budget Builder
startHere.why: A billion, eleven slots, real market values, no opponent. Choose this over Squad Deal if you want the maths rather than the luck of mystery boxes, and over Fantasy Draft if you would rather not have an AI taking your first choice off the board.

startHere.label: Soccer Grid
startHere.why: The 3x3 board, where a correct answer is only worth what nobody else picked. It tests whether you actually know who played where rather than who is famous, so it is the right pick once the single answer puzzles start feeling too easy.

draft.reference: Almost everything in this section runs on the transfer market, so it is worth knowing how that actually works. European clubs can only register signings inside two windows, a long one across the summer and a short one in January. Since the Bosman ruling in 1995, a player whose contract has run out can move for no fee at all, which is why clubs would rather sell someone with a year left than lose him for nothing. And the fee is only half the cost: it is a one-off payment to the selling club, while wages are paid every week for the length of the deal and often add up to more. The published numbers are estimates too. Fees frequently go undisclosed and add-ons sit inside the headline figure, and Neymar's 222 million euro move from Barcelona to Paris Saint-Germain in 2017 still sits at the top of the list.
referenceFacts: European clubs can only register new signings during transfer windows, a longer one over the summer and a shorter one in January.
The Bosman ruling in 1995 established that a player whose contract has expired can move to another club without a transfer fee being paid.
A common consequence of that ruling is clubs choosing to sell players who have a year left on their contract rather than losing them for nothing at expiry.
A transfer fee is a one-off payment made to the selling club.
Player wages are paid throughout the length of the contract and often total more than the transfer fee itself.
Many transfer fees are never officially disclosed, and reported figures commonly bundle in performance-based add-ons, so published values are estimates rather than confirmed amounts.
Neymar moved from Barcelona to Paris Saint-Germain in 2017 for 222 million euros.
That 222 million euro fee is still the highest transfer fee ever paid for a footballer.

faqs.q: Do I need to follow more than the Premier League?
faqs.a: No, but the further you look the more of this opens up. The guessing games lean on players who moved around the big European leagues, so if the Premier League is your limit you will still recognise most of them. Club Manager is the one that rewards breadth, since it covers 330 real clubs across 20 leagues and you can sit in whichever one you actually watch. If a puzzle throws up a name you have never heard of, there is another one along in a second.

faqs.q: How up to date are the players and the values?
faqs.a: Squads and valuations come from real data that gets refreshed in batches rather than live, so in the days after a big move a player can still be sitting at his old club. The historical games are out of date on purpose: Club Manager lets you start in a real past season, and Player Stock Market buys you in at that year's real prices, which is the whole point of it.

faqs.q: I have five minutes. Which one?
faqs.a: Alphabet Sprint, one player per letter against the clock, is the fastest thing in here. Footle is a single player from a stat line. Rarity Round is the strange one: you are not trying to be right, you are trying to be the only person who said it, so the obvious answer is the losing answer.

faqs.q: Which of these is worth a whole evening?
faqs.a: Soccer Career if you want to be the player, from a boyhood club through the money and the bad decisions to retirement. Club Manager if you want the dugout instead, with negotiations, board objectives and the sack race hanging over you. Stadium Tycoon and Wonderkid Factory are the idle ones, they keep ticking while you are doing something else, so they suit a second tab better than an hour of full attention.

problems: FACTS / referenceFacts[0] and reference prose. "European clubs can only register new signings during transfer windows, a longer one over the summer and a shorter one in January." The word "only" is false. Under the FIFA registration rules a professional whose contract expired before the end of a registration period may be registered outside it, which is why leagues sign free agents out of window (the Premier League gives clubs extra days after deadline day for exactly this). The mirrored line in the reference paragraph, "European clubs can only register signings inside two windows", carries the same error. Reject until qualified.

FACTS / referenceFacts[3]. "A transfer fee is a one-off payment made to the selling club." Stated flatly this is wrong. Fees are routinely paid in instalments over several years, and the draft's own example proves it: the Neymar 222 million euro deal was structured with a deferred payment and a large variable component. It also sits against referenceFacts[5], which says add-ons are bundled into the headline figure, meaning part of the fee is contingent and paid later. The point the writer wants (one-time cost versus a recurring weekly one) is fine, the absolute wording is not.

FACTS / referenceFacts[1]. "The Bosman ruling in 1995 established that a player whose contract has expired can move to another club without a transfer fee being paid." Over-broad as a standalone fact. The December 1995 European Court of Justice ruling applied to EU nationals moving between clubs in different EU member states; the general out-of-contract free move was carried into the transfer regulations afterwards. The popular shorthand is defensible in the prose paragraph, but referenceFacts is presented as a list of discrete verified facts and this one needs its scope.

FACTS / referenceFacts[7] and reference prose. "That 222 million euro fee is still the highest transfer fee ever paid for a footballer." This is TRUE as of today, verified: the all-time list still has Neymar at the top and nothing in the 2026 summer window came near it (the biggest 2026 deals landed around 117 million pounds). The problem is durability, not accuracy. Every route on this site ships as a frozen snapshot held for weeks, the word "still" is a claim about today, and the European window has not shut yet. Either drop "still" and date the claim, or accept that the page can go stale without anyone touching it.

GAME CLAIMS / faqs[2].a. "Rarity Round is the strange one: you are not trying to be right, you are trying to be the only person who said it, so the obvious answer is the losing answer." Wrong on both counts against src/pages/RarityRound.tsx. Its own rules say "Search for and pick any real, valid answer" and "Score is based on how obscure your answer is within the category's full pool of valid answers", ranked by fame inside a data pool. Nothing measures what other players said. You very much are trying to be right. The game also carries a Crowd Says mode where the most famous answer wins, which is the exact inverse of the sentence.

GAME CLAIMS / whyHere. "Soccer Grid, Connections and Transfer Path make you hold two things at once, a club and a season, or two players and the ground they once shared." Soccer Grid has no season criterion. src/data/soccerGridPuzzles.ts shows the attribute types are club, position, league, award and competition ("Played for Barcelona" crossed with "Forward", "Champions League Winner", "World Cup Winner"). The club-and-season pairing belongs to Transfer Path, not the grid. Connections also does not fit either shape described: it is finding groups of four connected players.

GAME CLAIMS / startHere[3].why (/soccer-grid). "The 3x3 board, where a correct answer is only worth what nobody else picked." Overstates. The mechanic is right (rarity is the share of players who picked the same answer: under 5 percent rare, 5 to 25 percent uncommon, over 25 percent standard) but the score is correct cells out of nine alongside a rarity percentage. Rarity grades the answer, it is not the whole of its worth.

GAME CLAIMS / startHere[1].why (/club-manager, on Rebuild). "Rebuild Challenge scratches the same itch in a fraction of the time, one club in trouble and a set of cuts you have to commit to." src/pages/Rebuild.tsx lets you pick any of 63 real clubs, "Tiers run from elite (Real Madrid, Arsenal) to modest (Southampton, Genk)", so the club is not in trouble by definition. "A set of cuts" also implies a batch decision, while the game spins one XI position at a time and asks keep or sell on each.

GAME CLAIMS / whyHere against faqs[3].a. Internal contradiction on Stadium Tycoon. whyHere: "Soccer Career, Club Manager and Stadium Tycoon are not puzzles at all, they are evenings." faqs[3].a: "Stadium Tycoon and Wonderkid Factory are the idle ones ... so they suit a second tab better than an hour of full attention." The same page tells the reader to give it an evening and then not to. Pick one.

GAME CLAIMS / whyHere. "Then the money games, which in soccer means fees and auctions rather than draft picks." The soccer section contains Fantasy Draft, Gauntlet Draft and Dart Draft, and the page itself recommends Fantasy Draft two paragraphs later in startHere[2].why. The contrast is false on its own page.

VOICE / intro closing sentence and whyHere opener. No banned filler anywhere (no "dive into", "elevate", "unleash", "look no further"), but two sentences would work unchanged under any sport: "All of it is free and plays in the browser without an account." and "The split that matters here is how long you want to sit down for." Low severity, both are true and useful, flagged per the brief.

VOICE / intro. "and the one that gets rebuilt most often" is a development-history claim about the repo, not about the games. A visitor cannot check it and it reads as dev-log talk in cornerstone copy. Suggest cutting the clause.
correctedFacts: Transfer windows: "European clubs register new signings during two windows, a longer one over the summer and a shorter one in January. The main exception is a player already out of contract, who can generally be signed and registered outside a window."
Transfer fee: "A transfer fee is paid to the selling club as a one-time cost rather than a recurring one, though it is often spread across instalments over several years."

Bosman: "The Bosman ruling in 1995 established freedom of movement for out-of-contract players inside the EU, and the principle that a player whose contract has expired can move without a fee was carried into the transfer regulations that followed."

Neymar record (verified accurate, keep the fact, fix the framing): "Neymar's 222 million euro move from Barcelona to Paris Saint-Germain in 2017 is the highest transfer fee ever paid for a footballer." Drop the word "still", which decays on a frozen page.

Rarity Round: "You still have to name a real, valid answer. The score is how obscure your pick is inside the category's pool, so the obvious answer is the low-scoring one. There is a Crowd Says mode that flips it and rewards the most famous answer."
Soccer Grid: "Soccer Grid crosses a club against a second condition, a position, a league, a trophy or an award, and grades every correct cell by how many other players picked the same name."

Rebuild Challenge: "Rebuild Challenge scratches the same itch in a fraction of the time: pick one of 63 real clubs, elite or modest, then spin through your XI one shirt at a time and decide who you keep and who you sell."

Verified true and needing no change: the 1995 date for Bosman, clubs selling players with a year left rather than losing them for nothing, wages over a long contract often totalling more than the fee, fees going undisclosed with add-ons bundled into reported figures, the Neymar move itself (Barcelona to Paris Saint-Germain, 2017, 222 million euros), and "more than thirty games" (the registry carries 40 under Soccer, the approved list 31).

Verified true against the code, needing no change: Career Ladder does hand back career stops in order (src/lib/careerLadder.ts sorts by sortOrder), and both idle games really do progress while you are away (Stadium Tycoon offlineEarnings; Wonderkid Factory ticks offline at half speed, capped at eight hours).

PATHS are clean: /career-ladder, /club-manager, /budget-builder and /soccer-grid all appear exactly in the approved list. DASHES are clean: no em dash or en dash anywhere in the draft. RIVALS are clean: no rival site, app or game name, and the word "immaculate" does not appear.

draft.intro: Ten pro football games live here and they are not variations on one idea. One hands you a real cap sheet and a draft board, one blanks a single name out of a Super Bowl starting lineup, and one repaints the map of America every week until a single team owns it. All of them play signed out and free, so you can bounce between them until one sticks.
draft.whyHere: Half of this page puts you inside the building. NFL Front Office is the desk job: 32 real clubs, a hard cap, trade partners who hang up on you, an owner who fires you when the mandate slips. NFL My Career runs the same league from the locker room, eight positions, and an envelope you can take if you are willing to be investigated for it. 17-0 Perfect Season drafts one cross era offense off a wheel of real team seasons and simulates whether it runs the table. The rest are short: NFL Grid, NFL Connections, NFL Connect 4, NFL Career Path and NFL Higher or Lower are recall in five different shapes, Missing Eleven needs ninety seconds to make you doubt a game you watched live, and NFL Conquest plays a season as a land grab.

startHere.label: NFL Front Office
startHere.why: The GM chair, and the only one here that runs for as many seasons as you can survive. Real rosters against a hard cap, trades where the other side counters or hangs up, draft grades that lie to you. NFL My Career is the same league from a player's seat, and 17-0 Perfect Season is one team drafted for one run.

startHere.label: NFL My Career
startHere.why: Pick this if the roster spreadsheet is the boring part. You create a prospect, a real team drafts you, and each season hands you one decision: the surgery or the season, the money or the contender, the envelope or the phone call reporting it. Front Office asks how you build a team. This asks what you do at 28 when the knee starts talking.

startHere.label: NFL Grid
startHere.why: The five minute daily. Every cell has to satisfy its row and its column at the same time, so Packers crossed with Super Bowl winner needs a man who did both, and the rarity score means a forgotten journeyman beats an obvious Hall of Famer. NFL Connections points the same knowledge at grouping, NFL Connect 4 turns it into a two player board.

startHere.label: Missing Eleven
startHere.why: The quickest one and the meanest. A genuine Super Bowl starting lineup with one name blanked, three guesses, and the famous player you are about to type was very often watching the kickoff from the sideline. NFL Career Path feeds you clues about a hidden player. This gives you his ten teammates and makes you work backwards.

draft.reference: Pro football's structure points at parity. Thirty two teams sit in two conferences, the AFC and the NFC, split into four divisions of four, every club works under the same hard salary cap, and the draft runs in reverse order of the previous season's standings. The regular season grew from 16 games to 17 in 2021 and is still the shortest of the major American leagues, which is why one loss matters here in a way it cannot across 82 or 162. The postseason is the only one of those leagues that is single elimination the whole way through: 14 teams since the 2020 season, seven per conference, and only the top seed in each gets the opening weekend off. Which is why 1972 still stands alone. Don Shula's Dolphins won all 14 regular season games and all three in the playoffs, beating Washington 14-7 in Super Bowl VII, and nobody has finished a season unbeaten since.
referenceFacts: The NFL has 32 teams.
The teams are divided into two conferences, the AFC and the NFC.
Each conference is split into four divisions of four teams each.
The NFL operates a hard salary cap that applies to every club.
The NFL draft order runs in reverse order of the previous season's standings.
The NFL regular season expanded from 16 games to 17 games in 2021.
The NFL regular season is the shortest of the major American professional leagues, compared with 82 games in the NBA and NHL and 162 in MLB.
The NFL postseason is single elimination in every round, the only major American league postseason that is.
The playoff field has been 14 teams, seven per conference, since the 2020 season.
Only the top seed in each conference receives a first round bye under that format.
The 1972 Miami Dolphins were coached by Don Shula.
The 1972 Dolphins won all 14 of their regular season games.
The 1972 Dolphins won all three of their postseason games.
The 1972 Dolphins beat Washington 14-7 in Super Bowl VII.
No NFL team has completed an unbeaten season since 1972; the Dolphins remain the only one.

faqs.q: Which one is the proper franchise mode?
faqs.a: NFL Front Office. You take one of the 32 clubs and run it for as many seasons as ownership lets you: cap sheet, cuts, free agency, trade calls that get countered or hung up on, and a 40 prospect draft class where the scouting grade can be off by four points either way. It saves in your browser after every move, and yes, you can get fired. If you want the same league from a player's seat, that is NFL My Career.

faqs.q: Is there a daily puzzle here, or is it all endless?
faqs.a: Both. NFL Grid, NFL Career Path, NFL Connections, NFL Higher or Lower, Missing Eleven and NFL Conquest all deal one shared puzzle a day that resets at midnight Eastern, so everyone is working on the same thing that day. Each of them also has an unlimited mode for when the daily is not enough.

faqs.q: I have only really watched since about 2010. Am I going to be lost?
faqs.a: Not on most of them. NFL Higher or Lower only uses careers that started in 2000 or later, NFL Front Office runs current rosters, and the 17-0 Perfect Season wheel starts at 1999. NFL Grid and Missing Eleven are the two that reach further back, and they are the ones where you actually pick something up.

faqs.q: Why are there no team logos, helmets or player photos?
faqs.a: Because all of that is licensed and this is an independent fan project with no connection to the league. The names, the stats and the Super Bowl lineups are real and checked. The badges are simply not here, and nothing on the page pretends otherwise.

problems: FACTS / GAME CLAIMS (blocking). faqs[4].a: "The names, the stats and the Super Bowl lineups are real and checked." This is false, and it is false in the one answer whose whole job is telling a visitor what is real. Two of the three games the page leads with use deliberately invented names. src/lib/frontOffice.ts:448 is headed "Draft (fictional prospects, clearly generated)" and prospectName() builds every draft prospect and free agent from 34 invented first names by 34 invented last names (Jalen Whitfield, Marcus Calloway, Rashad Fenwick), checked against a "real-name wall" by simInventedNames precisely so they are NOT real people. NFL My Career is the same: the draft's own startHere entry says "You create a prospect" two paragraphs earlier, so the FAQ contradicts the page above it. The stats and the Super Bowl lineups ARE real and checked (src/lib/missingEleven.ts carries a documented two-source verification, Chrome-rendered pro-football-reference starters tables cross-checked against Wikipedia starting lineups, 22/22 on SB LI), so only "the names" is wrong. Fix rather than delete.

GAME CLAIMS (blocking). whyHere: "Half of this page puts you inside the building." It is not half. The same paragraph then names three games (NFL Front Office, NFL My Career, 17-0 Perfect Season) and sweeps the other seven into "The rest are short". Three of ten.

GAME CLAIMS (blocking). whyHere: "an envelope you can take if you are willing to be investigated for it." Wrong verb, wrong direction. The only envelope in NFL My Career is src/lib/nflCareerCorruption.ts:130, "The envelope in the meeting room": a defensive bounty pool that a veteran passes down the row, and the corrupt option is "Put in and play the game", whose result line is "You put your money in the envelope." You pay into it, you never take anything out of it. The investigation half of the sentence is sound (that choice sets heat +18, and heat at or above 90 opens a formal league investigation and a suspended season), so only the taking is invented.

GAME CLAIMS (blocking). startHere[1] (/nfl-my-career) why: "the envelope or the phone call reporting it." There is no phone call. The third option on that crossroad is "Tell the coach it stops today" (src/lib/nflCareerCorruption.ts:142). Invented detail in a place the copy is otherwise precise.

GAME CLAIMS (fix before ship). startHere[0] (/front-office) why: "the only one here that runs for as many seasons as you can survive." Overclaimed superlative. NFL My Career also runs season after season and can also be ended early against your will (suspendedSeasons, src/lib/nflMyCareer.ts:227, "means the next season is served banned"). Front Office is the open-ended one, My Career ends at retirement, but "the only one" as written is not true.

GAME CLAIMS (minor). faqs[1].a: "Each of them also has an unlimited mode for when the daily is not enough." True for five of the six, but NFL Conquest's second mode is not called that anywhere a player can see: ImperialismBoard.tsx types it 'daily' | 'free' and the page offers Imperialism and Arcade. Functionally accurate, but a visitor hunting for an "unlimited" button on /conquest will not find one. Suggest "free play" so the copy matches the screen.

VOICE (minor). intro, final sentence: "All of them play signed out and free, so you can bounce between them until one sticks." Works unchanged on the NBA, MLB and NHL pages. It is the sitewide pitch, not something about pro football.

VOICE (minor). faqs[1].a: strip the game names out of "all deal one shared puzzle a day that resets at midnight Eastern, so everyone is working on the same thing that day. Each of them also has an unlimited mode for when the daily is not enough" and nothing sport-specific is left. Template answer.
correctedFacts: All 15 entries in referenceFacts are true as written and none need correcting. Confirmed against sources: 32 teams in the AFC and NFC, eight divisions of four, hard cap; 16 to 17 games in 2021 (NFL owners approved the 17th game for 2021 under the 2020 CBA); shortest major American regular season against 82 in the NBA and NHL and 162 in MLB; single elimination in every round, unique among the four; 14-team field, seven per conference, since the 2020 season, with only the top seed in each conference taking the bye; Don Shula's 1972 Dolphins 14-0 in the regular season, 3-0 in the playoffs, beat Washington 14-7 in Super Bowl VII, still the only unbeaten season in NFL history. The reference prose adds no claim the facts list does not carry.

referenceFacts[4], "The NFL draft order runs in reverse order of the previous season's standings", is a fair summary and passes, but note it is a simplification: the last 14 slots are set by how far a playoff team advanced, then by reverse record within each elimination round, not by standings alone. It matches the NFL's own framing ("reverse order of finish in the previous season"), so no change is required.

faqs[4].a should read something like: "The real players, their stats and the Super Bowl lineups are real and checked. The draft prospects in Front Office and the player you create in My Career are made up on purpose, and they are checked against real names so they stay made up."
whyHere should read something like: "...an envelope that gets passed down the row, and a league investigation if you put money in it."
whyHere's opening should read "Three of these put you inside the building" rather than "Half of this page".

faqs.q: Why do so many of these games use per 36 minute numbers instead of per game averages?
faqs.a: Because the historical season records store totals and minutes rather than game counts, so a per 36 rate is exact where a per game average would be an estimate. It also puts eras on one scale, since the 1960s were played at a much higher pace and per game numbers from then flatter everybody. /stat-detective and /nba-stat-line both work in per 36 for that reason.

faqs.q: Why will some games not let me pick seasons from the 1960s?
faqs.a: Because the stat being asked for did not exist yet. Steals and blocks were not official until 1973-74 and the three point line arrived in 1979-80, so when a target in /nba-stat-line includes one of those, older seasons have no honest number to contribute and sit out. Targets without them open the pool back to 1951-52.

faqs.q: How much of this is real data and how much is invented?
faqs.a: The players, the seasons and the careers are real throughout. /missing-five checks every lineup against the official box score of that exact game, and /nba-grid and /nba-connections verify answers against career records. The two long sims are the stated exceptions: your player in /nba-my-career is fictional by design, and the contracts, salaries and ages in /nba-front-office are invented numbers wrapped around real players.

faqs.q: Which of these have a daily puzzle?
faqs.a: Plenty of them. /nba-grid, /nba-connections, /missing-five, /nba-higher-lower and /nba-stat-line serve everyone the same board once a day, and /perfect-season-nba, /perfect-lineup-nba, /nba-career and /conquest-nba have daily modes too. They all roll over at midnight Eastern. The rest, /nba-connect-4 and /nba-chain included, you can just keep playing.

draft.intro: Fifteen NBA games sit on this page, and most of them start from a box score rather than a highlight. Basketball only puts five men on the floor at once, which is why a starting five is the kind of thing people argue about at a bar and why one per 36 line is often enough to name a whole career. The season data behind all of it is real and goes back to 1951-52, so a 1962 center and last year's rookie turn up in the same puzzle.
draft.reference: Basketball's record book has hard start dates, and a lot of the sport's arguments trace back to them. The NBA adopted the 24 second shot clock for the 1954-55 season, which is the line between the modern game and the stalling contests before it. Steals, blocks and the split between offensive and defensive rebounds only became official statistics in 1973-74, and individual turnovers waited until 1977-78, which is why Bill Russell and Wilt Chamberlain carry no official career block totals despite both being remembered as dominant shot blockers. The three point line came in for 1979-80, originally as a one year trial. And the 82 game season only started in 1967-68, the year expansion took the league to twelve teams. So compare eras all you like, but for some whole careers the numbers people want were simply never written down.
referenceFacts: The NBA adopted the 24 second shot clock for the 1954-55 season.
Before the shot clock, teams could stall by holding the ball, and games were far lower scoring.
Steals and blocks first became official NBA statistics in the 1973-74 season.
The split between offensive and defensive rebounds also became official in 1973-74.
Individual player turnovers did not become an official NBA statistic until 1977-78.
Bill Russell and Wilt Chamberlain both finished their careers before 1973-74, so neither has an official career block total.
Bill Russell and Wilt Chamberlain are both widely remembered as dominant shot blockers.
The three point line was adopted by the NBA for the 1979-80 season.
The three point line was introduced initially as a one year trial.
The NBA first played an 82 game regular season in 1967-68.
The 1967-68 expansion took the NBA to twelve teams.

startHere.label: NBA Career Path
startHere.why: The softest landing in the section. You get a position and a pot of 1,000 points, wrong guesses cost nothing, and you decide how many clues you can afford to buy. If you want the same idea with no safety net, /stat-detective hands you a bare stat line and no clue shop.

startHere.label: Stat Detective
startHere.why: For people who actually read box scores. All you get is a decade, a position and a per 36 line, and eight guesses to work out who put it up. Harder than /nba-career because nothing is spoon fed, and the pool runs well past the household names.

startHere.label: NBA Franchise Grid
startHere.why: The two minute daily. Nine cells, nine guesses, so a single miss ends any perfect board, and it is pure recall of who played where. Take /nba-connections instead if you would rather sort twenty names into hidden groups than dig up one player per square.

startHere.label: NBA Front Office
startHere.why: The one that eats an evening. A real rotation, a cap sheet, a trade engine that haggles back, and an owner who can fire you. Go to /nba-my-career instead if you would rather live one player's twenty years than run the whole building.

draft.whyHere: Four things go on in here. Some games hand you numbers and want the name back: /stat-detective scrubs the name off a real per 36 season, /nba-career sells you clues at 150 points a go, and /missing-five blanks one starter out of a genuine Finals box score. Some are boards you earn a square at a time, like the nine cells of /nba-grid or the twenty names of /nba-connections. Some make you assemble a five under awkward rules, which is /nba-starting-5 with its random franchises and /perfect-season-nba with its draft wheel. And some run for years: /nba-front-office gives you a cap sheet and 29 rivals, while /nba-my-career takes an invented rookie from draft night to the rafters.

problems: startHere[1] (/stat-detective) .why — FALSE game claim. Exact text: "All you get is a decade, a position and a per 36 line, and eight guesses to work out who put it up. Harder than /nba-career because nothing is spoon fed". src/lib/statDetective.ts hintsFor() (lines 440-448) hands out a FREE clue after every single miss: career span at 1 miss, surname initial at 2, career franchise count at 3, the team at 4, first-name initial at 5, and the EXACT SEASON at 6. The page also returns era/position/franchise feedback chips after each guess. So "all you get is" is false and "nothing is spoon fed" is the opposite of what the code does. The stated reason it is harder than /nba-career is also backwards: /nba-career charges 150 points per clue, /stat-detective gives six of them away for nothing.

startHere[0] (/nba-career) .why — same false premise carried over. Exact text: "If you want the same idea with no safety net, /stat-detective hands you a bare stat line and no clue shop." "No clue shop" is literally true (nothing is purchased) but "no safety net" is wrong for the reason above: /stat-detective's safety net is automatic and free.

whyHere — misdescribes /perfect-season-nba. Exact text: "Some make you assemble a five under awkward rules, which is /nba-starting-5 with its random franchises and /perfect-season-nba with its draft wheel." Perfect Season drafts SIX, not five. Its own registry description says "draft a six man rotation" and src/pages/PerfectSeasonNBA.tsx line 829 reads "Repeat until all 6 slots are filled: point guard, shooting guard, small forward, power forward, center, and a sixth man who can be anyone." Grouping it under "assemble a five" contradicts the game's own copy.

startHere[2] (/nba-grid) .why — misdescribes the puzzle. Exact text: "it is pure recall of who played where". Only some axes are franchises. src/pages/NbaGrid.tsx line 229: "Rows and columns are franchises a player's career touched, or career milestones like 10,000+ points", and line 423 confirms milestones like 10,000 points, 5,000 rebounds or 900 games played. "Pure recall of who played where" leaves out half the board.

startHere[3] (/nba-front-office) .why — VOICE, generic across sports. Exact text: "A real rotation, a cap sheet, a trade engine that haggles back, and an owner who can fire you." Every clause is true verbatim of /nhl-front-office and /mlb-front-office, which run the same shared engine (src/components/front-office-shared, src/lib/foOwnerMandate). Nothing in the sentence is basketball. It would ship unchanged on the hockey or baseball page.
correctedFacts: /stat-detective: the honest version is that it gives you a decade, a position and a per 36 line to start, eight guesses, and a free clue after every miss that ends with the exact season handed over on miss six. It is not a no-clues game; the difference from /nba-career is that the clues arrive automatically instead of being bought.
/perfect-season-nba: you draft six, a starting five plus a sixth man who can be anyone, not five.
/nba-grid: the rows and columns mix franchises a career touched with career milestones (10,000+ points, 5,000 rebounds, 900 games played), so it is not purely who-played-where recall.

draft.intro: Ten baseball games here, and most of them run on the stuff fans argue about anyway: who hit more home runs, who passed through which clubhouse, which nine names got written on a World Series lineup card. Six are daily, so there is a fresh one sitting there most mornings. The other four are the long ones, where a sitting costs you a season or a whole career.
draft.whyHere: Three shapes, roughly. Straight recall: MLB Higher or Lower is one question on a loop (which legend hit more career home runs), Career Path walks a player's stops until you can name him, and Missing Nine hands you eight of the nine in a famous World Series order and lets the gap do the work. Puzzles that make you hold two facts at once: MLB Franchise Grid wants somebody who suited up for both teams in a square, Connections wants the thread joining four names, MLB Connect 4 buries trivia under the discs. Then the sims, where one sitting is a season or a life: MLB Front Office runs a club down to the tax line, MLB My Career runs one player you create, 162-0 Perfect Season drafts across eras, and MLB Conquest turns the standings into a land grab.

startHere.label: Career Path
startHere.why: Start here if you just want to guess a player. It feeds you his stops one at a time and you narrow it down, so being wrong early costs you nothing and you still get there. Missing Nine, the other guessing game, expects you to already know a specific famous team.

startHere.label: Missing Nine
startHere.why: For the fan who remembers teams rather than individual careers. You get a real World Series batting order with one starter blanked out, so the other eight names around the hole are your clue and October history does the heavy lifting.

startHere.label: MLB Franchise Grid
startHere.why: Take this over Connections if you like the crossword shape. Every square has to satisfy two franchises at once, which quietly makes a well travelled journeyman more useful than the biggest name you know. Connections is the opposite job: work out what four players already have in common.

startHere.label: MLB Front Office
startHere.why: The long one to pick if you would rather run the club than be the player: real 2026 rosters, payroll against the tax line, deadline trades, October, then doing it again next year. MLB My Career is its mirror image, one player you create from draft day, and 162-0 Perfect Season is neither, a draft across eras chasing an unbeaten season no real team has ever had.

draft.reference: Baseball still has no game clock. A pitch clock arrived in 2023 and pulled the average nine inning game down to roughly two hours 40 minutes, but nothing counts down to zero: the defense has to record 27 outs, three an inning over nine, and a team in front cannot sit on a lead. The infield is fixed by rule, 90 feet between bases and the pitching rubber 60 feet 6 inches from home, a distance the National League set in 1893 and nobody has moved since. Past the infield nothing is standard, which is why the left field wall at Fenway Park, the Green Monster, stands about 37 feet tall barely 310 feet down the line. The season runs 162 games, the length the American League adopted in 1961 and the National League in 1962.
referenceFacts: Baseball has no game clock governing the length of a game.
MLB introduced a pitch clock in the 2023 season.
The average nine inning MLB game in 2023 was about two hours and 40 minutes, down roughly 24 minutes from 2022.
A nine inning game requires the fielding side to record 27 outs, three per inning across nine innings.
Because there is no clock, a leading team cannot run time out; it must still record the remaining outs.
The bases in MLB are 90 feet apart.
The pitching rubber is 60 feet 6 inches from home plate.
The National League established the 60 feet 6 inches pitching distance in 1893 and it has not changed since.
MLB does not standardise outfield dimensions, so ballpark outfields differ from each other.
The left field wall at Fenway Park is nicknamed the Green Monster.
The Green Monster is about 37 feet tall (37 feet 2 inches).
The Green Monster sits about 310 feet from home plate down the left field line.
The MLB regular season is 162 games.
The American League moved to a 162 game schedule in 1961.
The National League moved to a 162 game schedule in 1962.
No MLB team has ever completed an unbeaten 162 game season.

faqs.q: Which of these reset every day?
faqs.a: Six of the ten. Career Path, MLB Higher or Lower, MLB Franchise Grid, MLB Conquest, Missing Nine and Connections all serve a new puzzle each day. 162-0 Perfect Season, MLB Connect 4, MLB My Career and MLB Front Office are not on a clock, so you start those whenever you want.

faqs.q: Do I need to know old baseball for these?
faqs.a: For some of them, yes. MLB Higher or Lower, Missing Nine and MLB Franchise Grid pull from the whole history of the sport, so the answer is often somebody who retired before you were born. If you only follow the current game, start with MLB Front Office, which runs on real 2026 rosters, or MLB My Career, where the player is one you invent.

faqs.q: What is the actual difference between MLB Front Office and MLB My Career?
faqs.a: Scope. Front Office is the whole club: payroll against the tax line, trades, a playoff run, then building the next one. My Career is one person. You name him, give him one of 11 positions from starting pitcher to designated hitter, and steer him through the crossroads from the draft toward Cooperstown.

faqs.q: Are the players real?
faqs.a: In the guessing games, yes. Real players, real career stops, nothing made up to fill a gap, and no words put in anybody's mouth. In MLB My Career the player is yours, created at the start, so that story belongs to you rather than to somebody who actually lived it.

problems: GAME CLAIMS (intro, false and self-contradicting): "The other four are the long ones, where a sitting costs you a season or a whole career." The registry (src/data/gameRegistry.ts lines 194-203) marks exactly six daily, so the other four are 162-0 Perfect Season, MLB Connect 4, MLB My Career and MLB Front Office. MLB Connect 4 is a short trivia game ("Baseball trivia meets Connect 4"), not a season or a career. Only three of the four are long. The draft's own faqs[0] lists that same four, so the intro contradicts the FAQ.

GAME CLAIMS (whyHere): "Then the sims, where one sitting is a season or a life: MLB Front Office runs a club down to the tax line, MLB My Career runs one player you create, 162-0 Perfect Season drafts across eras, and MLB Conquest turns the standings into a land grab." Two errors. MLB Conquest is one of the six DAILY games (daily: true in the registry, and the draft's own FAQ lists it as daily), so putting it in the non-daily sim bucket contradicts the FAQ and the intro. And it is not driven by standings: you pick a team, predict each round's game, and simulated results redraw a 58-territory map (src/data/conquestDataMlb.ts, src/hooks/useConquest.ts).

GAME CLAIMS (faqs[1], false for Missing Nine): "MLB Higher or Lower, Missing Nine and MLB Franchise Grid pull from the whole history of the sport, so the answer is often somebody who retired before you were born." Missing Nine's entire pool is ten lineups from five World Series games, 1986, 1988, 2001, 2013 and 2016 (src/lib/missingNine.ts, ids ws-1986-g6-bos through ws-2016-g7-cle). Nothing before 1986 exists in it, and the 2016 Cubs and Cleveland lineups contain players still active in 2026 (Kyle Schwarber, Willson Contreras). True for MLB Higher or Lower, whose pool is retired-only by construction (src/data/mlbHLPlayers.ts).

FACTS (referenceFacts, overstated): "MLB does not standardise outfield dimensions, so ballpark outfields differ from each other." And the same overstatement in reference: "Past the infield nothing is standard." Rule 2.01 does set minimums for any field constructed after June 1, 1958 (325 feet down each foul line, 400 feet to center) and bars remodels below them. The defensible claim is that MLB prescribes no exact outfield dimensions, grandfathers pre-1958 parks like Fenway, and has waived the minimums, so parks differ.

GAME CLAIMS (startHere[0].why, misdescribes the mechanic): "It feeds you his stops one at a time and you narrow it down." Career Path's ladder is Position, then Draft, then First Team, then career teams added one at a time, then Career Stats, then Awards (src/hooks/useBaseballCareer.ts). Career stops are only the middle of a six-rung clue ladder. The rest of that sentence is correct: a wrong guess neither advances the clue level nor deducts score, so "being wrong early costs you nothing" checks out.

VOICE (startHere[0].why, generic): "Start here if you just want to guess a player. It feeds you his stops one at a time and you narrow it down, so being wrong early costs you nothing and you still get there." Nothing in those two sentences is baseball. They would run unchanged on the soccer, NBA, NFL or NHL page. Only the trailing Missing Nine sentence anchors the entry to this sport.
correctedFacts: Non-daily baseball games are 162-0 Perfect Season, MLB Connect 4, MLB My Career and MLB Front Office. MLB Conquest is daily. The long-sitting games are three: 162-0 Perfect Season, MLB My Career and MLB Front Office.
Missing Nine draws on ten lineups from five World Series games: 1986, 1988, 2001, 2013 and 2016. Its oldest answers are from 1986 and several 2016 answers are players still active in 2026.

MLB Rule 2.01 requires any playing field built after June 1, 1958 to be at least 325 feet from home plate down each foul line and 400 feet to center field, with pre-1958 parks such as Fenway exempt and waivers granted since. MLB prescribes no exact outfield dimensions, which is why parks differ.
Career Path reveals, in order: Position, Draft, First Team, career teams one at a time, Career Stats, Awards.

MLB Conquest: you pick a team, predict its game each round, and the simulated results for all 30 clubs redraw a 58-territory map, with the winner annexing the loser's whole empire. Toronto and San Diego start landless.

Precision note, not an error: the 2 hours 40 minutes figure is specifically 2023. The average nine-inning game was 2:36 in 2024 and 2:38 in 2025, so the sentence stays true only because it is tied to 2023.

Precision note, not an error: 90 feet between bases is still the rule-book measurement, but the 18-inch bases introduced in 2023 cut the actual first-to-second and second-to-third paths by about 4.5 inches each.

Verified true: pitch clock introduced 2023; 2023 average 2:40, down about 24 minutes from 2022; 27 outs, three an inning over nine; pitching rubber 60 feet 6 inches, set by the National League in 1893 and unchanged; Green Monster nickname, 37 feet 2 inches tall, 310 feet down the left field line; 162-game season, AL from 1961 and NL from 1962; no team has ever gone unbeaten over a season.

Verified clean: all four startHere paths (/baseball-career, /missing-nine, /mlb-grid, /mlb-front-office) match the valid list exactly, labels included. No em dashes or en dashes anywhere (scanned for U+2010 to U+2015 and U+2212, zero hits). No rival product names and no use of "immaculate"; "Connections" is the site's own registry label and is not on the simNoRivalNames list. No marketing filler.

draft.intro: Eleven NHL games here, all free, none of them behind a login. Some are thirty seconds of squinting at clue chips, some are a fictional player's twenty two season career, and one hands you a real 2026-27 roster and a hard cap and then lets ownership fire you. What they all quietly assume is hockey memory: sweater numbers, journeymen defensemen, and the fact that the Nordiques and the Avalanche are the same franchise.
draft.whyHere: Eleven games, and they mostly split by how much of your evening they want. The quick ones are guessing games with different tempers: Puck Detective hides a player off a current roster and answers each of your eight guesses with five chips, Career Path gives you a position and then charges points for every clue you buy, Higher / Lower asks only who finished with more career points. NHL Franchise Grid and NHL Connections test breadth instead, nine cells against twenty names. The long ones simulate: NHL Front Office is a real 2026-27 roster under a hard cap, NHL My Career is one fictional player over twenty two seasons, NHL Conquest turns a season of results into a land grab. 82-0 Perfect Season and Perfect Lineup: NHL draft then simulate, and NHL Connect 4 needs a second person.

startHere.label: Puck Detective
startHere.why: Pick this if you watch the league right now. The answer is always somebody on a current roster, and every guess comes back with five chips (team, position, nationality, age, jersey number), so you narrow instead of fishing. Career Path is the same idea for people whose hockey is older than this season.

startHere.label: Career Path
startHere.why: The all-time version of the same puzzle. You open with nothing but a position and buy clues one at a time (country, draft, teams, stats, awards), each one shaving your score, so it rewards recognising a draft slot rather than knowing depth charts. Wrong guesses are free here, which Puck Detective's eight guess limit is not.

startHere.label: Perfect Lineup: NHL
startHere.why: Five minutes, and no season to sit through. Three of your six slots arrive locked to a franchise or a decade, you fill them from the all-time pool, and one simulated game hands back a letter grade. 82-0 Perfect Season is the longer cousin: a wheel decides your options for you and the sim plays all 82 games.

startHere.label: NHL Front Office
startHere.why: The one that eats an evening. Real 2026-27 rosters, a hard cap every move has to fit under, the loser point in the standings, a divisional bracket, and an owner who fires you for missing the mandate. Choose it over NHL My Career if you would rather build the roster than be a player on it.

draft.reference: Two things about the NHL trip up people arriving from other sports. First, not every game hands out the same number of points. A win is worth two whether it comes in regulation, overtime or a shootout, and the team that loses in overtime or a shootout still keeps one, so a game settled inside sixty minutes is worth two points in total and one that goes past it is worth three. Rule 84.2 adds a wrinkle: a club that pulls its goalie in overtime and then loses forfeits that point. Second, the playoffs drop the shootout entirely. Postseason overtime is 5-on-5 sudden death in full twenty minute periods, repeated until somebody scores, and sixteen teams play four best-of-seven rounds, sixteen wins in all, for the Stanley Cup, which is not remade each year for the new champion the way other North American trophies are but handed on with the winners' names engraved on its bands.
referenceFacts: In the NHL regular season a win is worth two standings points whether it comes in regulation, in overtime or in a shootout.
A team that loses in overtime or in a shootout still receives one standings point.
A regulation loss is worth zero standings points.
A game decided in regulation therefore distributes two standings points in total, while a game that reaches overtime distributes three.

NHL Rule 84.2 provides that a team which removes its goaltender in overtime and then loses the game while the goaltender is off forfeits the point it would otherwise have received for the overtime loss.
There is no shootout in the Stanley Cup playoffs.
Playoff overtime is played 5-on-5, sudden death, in full twenty minute periods, repeated until a goal is scored.
Sixteen teams qualify for the Stanley Cup playoffs.
The Stanley Cup playoffs consist of four rounds, each a best-of-seven series.
Winning the Stanley Cup requires sixteen playoff wins.
Unlike the championship trophies of the other major North American leagues, a new Stanley Cup is not manufactured each year for the new champion; the trophy is handed on to the next winner.
The names of winning players and staff are engraved onto the bands of the Stanley Cup.

faqs.q: Which of these use this season's players and which go all the way back?
faqs.a: Puck Detective picks from current NHL rosters, and NHL Front Office starts you on the real 2026-27 rosters. Career Path, NHL Franchise Grid, Higher / Lower and Perfect Lineup: NHL pull from an all-era career database instead, so a 1970s winger turns up as readily as anyone playing tonight.

faqs.q: Are goalies actually in these, or is it skaters only?
faqs.a: Goalies are in. 82-0 Perfect Season gives them their own slot and weights it heaviest of the six, Perfect Lineup: NHL has a G slot, and NHL My Career lets you play one, with wins and save percentage instead of points and a stretch as the backup before the crease is yours. In Puck Detective they live in the Hard pool. NHL Connect 4 has a goalies board, but goalies are missing from the name suggestions, so type the full name and press Enter.

faqs.q: Do relocated franchises count as the same club?
faqs.a: In NHL Connect 4 yes, and the rules say so outright: Nordiques answers count for the Avalanche, Whalers for the Hurricanes, Thrashers for the Jets. NHL My Career goes the other way with its 2006-07 throwback, a sealed thirty team league where the Thrashers are still in Atlanta and the Coyotes are still in Phoenix, and where you never meet a club that did not exist yet.

faqs.q: What is the difference between 82-0 Perfect Season and Perfect Lineup: NHL?
faqs.a: Who sets your limits, and how long the sim runs. Perfect Season spins a wheel that lands on a franchise and a decade, you take one player from whatever it gives you, and then it plays all 82 games hunting a perfect record. Perfect Lineup locks three of your six slots to a team or an era up front, lets you choose freely from the all-time pool, weights the result 80 percent talent and 20 percent chemistry, and grades a single game.

problems: faqs[1].a (goalies FAQ) — exact text: "In Puck Detective they live in the Hard pool." This misdescribes the game. Per src/lib/puckDetective.ts, the difficulty tiers are for "unlimited/practice play only" and "Daily mode always draws from the full pool" of 876 players. Goalies are in the default Normal pool and in every daily puzzle. They are merely CONCENTRATED in Hard (which pulls the 170 players unmatched in nhl_player_stats, "mostly goalies, who have no career points stat by definition") and EXCLUDED from Easy (points >= 250). As written, a reader concludes they must switch to Hard to ever meet a goalie, which is false.

intro — exact text: "some are a fictional player's twenty two season career"; and whyHere — exact text: "NHL My Career is one fictional player over twenty two seasons". Twenty two is the retirement CEILING, not the career length. src/lib/nhlMyCareer.ts line 667 retires on `c.ovr <= 63 || c.age >= (c.pos === 'G' ? 41 : 40) || c.seasons.length >= 22`, so careers ending on rating decline or age run shorter. Stating it as the career length oversells. Should read "up to twenty two seasons".

faqs[1].a (goalies FAQ) — exact text: "and a stretch as the backup before the crease is yours". Stated as certain, but src/lib/nhlMyCareer.ts nhlAssignRole gives goalies an immediate starter path: `if (c.ovr >= incumbent + 2) { c.role = 'starter'; return '📋 The veteran lost the crease in camp. You are the number one.'; }`. The backup opening is the usual case, not the guaranteed one.

reference — exact text: "Rule 84.2 adds a wrinkle: a club that pulls its goalie in overtime and then loses forfeits that point." The visible prose is looser than the rule, and looser than the draft's own referenceFacts entry, which correctly says "loses the game while the goaltender is off". The forfeit applies only if the team is scored on during the time the goaltender is removed; if the goalie returns at the next stoppage and the team loses later in overtime, the point is kept. There is also a delayed-penalty exception. As written the sentence is false for those cases.

NOT IN THE DRAFT, adjacent repo finding surfaced by the 'immaculate' check: src/lib/hockeyGrid.ts line 5, src/lib/mlbGrid.ts line 5 and src/lib/nbaGrid.ts line 5 each contain the comment text "Immaculate-Grid-style". scripts/simNoRivalNames.mjs line 71 bans the pattern 'immaculate ?grid', which matches a space or nothing but NOT a hyphen, so the fence is green while three source files name a rival product in comments — exactly what that harness header says it exists to prevent. The draft copy itself is clean of rival names.
correctedFacts: Puck Detective's goalies appear in the default Normal pool and in every daily puzzle; the Easy/Normal/Hard tiers apply to practice play only, with goalies excluded from Easy and concentrated in Hard.
NHL My Career runs up to twenty two seasons; careers also end early on rating decline (ovr 63 or below) or at age 40, 41 for goalies.
In NHL My Career a goalie usually opens as the backup, but a rating two or more above the incumbent takes the crease straight away.

NHL Rule 84.2: a team that removes its goaltender in overtime forfeits its standings point only if it loses while the goaltender is off the ice; the point is not forfeited by the act of pulling the goalie alone.

draft.intro: College sports has a memory problem built into it. The roster you learned in November can be half gone by spring, and the conference a school played in three years ago might not exist any more. The six games here lean into that instead of fighting it, from a daily 3x3 grid of football names to two full program sims that run recruiting classes and postseason brackets, and all of them play free without signing in.
draft.whyHere: Two of these take a couple of minutes and two of them will eat an evening. /college-grid wants a football player who fits a row and a column at once, Alabama plus Heisman winner, that sort of thing, so the deep bench beats the obvious name. /guess-the-college and /guess-cbb-team both drip clues out one at a time, region then conference then mascot then postseason history, except one roams across D1 schools generally and the other never leaves basketball. /cfb-higher-lower is the quick one, two quarterbacks and a single number. The sims sit at the far end: /cfb-dynasty runs a football program through NIL, the portal and the 12 team Playoff, while /cbb-dynasty does a basketball one through one and dones and a March bracket.

startHere.label: CFB Higher or Lower
startHere.why: Start here if you follow college football loosely rather than closely. It is two quarterbacks and one question, which one threw for more career college yards, and the answers are counterintuitive often enough that guessing on reputation gets you burned. Quickest thing in the section.

startHere.label: Guess The College
startHere.why: Clues arrive one at a time and you can guess whenever you like, so the score rewards nerve. It covers D1 schools broadly, region, conference, mascot and athletic history, which makes it the one to pick if you know campuses and nicknames better than you know any single sport.

startHere.label: Guess The CBB Program
startHere.why: Same clue by clue shape as Guess The College, but it never leaves college basketball, so the clues lean on tournament runs and program history instead of general school facts. Pick this one over its sibling if your knowledge is specifically hoops.

startHere.label: CFB Dynasty
startHere.why: The long one. You run a football program through recruiting, NIL money, the transfer portal and the 12 team Playoff, across seasons. Its twin /cbb-dynasty is the same idea on a basketball calendar with one and dones and a March bracket, so pick by which sport you actually sit down and watch.

draft.reference: Almost everything that makes college sports confusing right now arrived in the last few years. The NCAA transfer portal opened on October 15, 2018, and the NCAA's interim name, image and likeness policy took effect on July 1, 2021, so players could change schools and get paid within three years of each other. A judge gave final approval to the House v. NCAA settlement in June 2025, and schools could begin paying athletes directly from July 1, 2025. The map moved too: in 2024 the Pac-12 lost ten members to the Big Ten, Big 12 and ACC, leaving Oregon State and Washington State. Football's playoff went from four teams to twelve for the 2024 season, with first round games hosted by the higher seed rather than at a neutral bowl site. Basketball's bracket has been steadier, 68 teams since 2011, with 31 of those spots going to conference champions.
referenceFacts: The NCAA transfer portal launched on October 15, 2018.
The NCAA's interim name, image and likeness policy took effect on July 1, 2021, allowing athletes to earn from their NIL without losing eligibility.
A federal judge granted final approval to the House v. NCAA settlement in June 2025.
Schools could begin sharing revenue directly with athletes from July 1, 2025.
Ten Pac-12 members departed in 2024 for the Big Ten, the Big 12 and the ACC.
Oregon State and Washington State were the two schools remaining in the Pac-12 after the 2024 departures.
The College Football Playoff expanded from four teams to twelve beginning with the 2024 season.
College Football Playoff first round games are hosted by the higher seed rather than at a neutral bowl site.
The NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament has had 68 teams since 2011.
31 of the 68 NCAA men's basketball tournament spots are automatic bids for conference champions.

faqs.q: Guess The College and Guess The CBB Program look like the same game. Which one do I want?
faqs.a: They share the format, clues released one at a time until you guess, but not the subject. Guess The College spans D1 schools generally, so a clue can be about region, conference, mascot or athletic history. Guess The CBB Program stays inside college basketball, so its clues lean on tournament runs and program history. Know schools, start with the first. Know hoops, start with the second.

faqs.q: Do I need to know who is actually on rosters this season?
faqs.a: No. College Grid and CFB Higher or Lower run on career and program history, not this week's depth chart, and the guess games are about schools rather than current players. Given how fast rosters turn over since the portal opened, a game built on current names would be stale in a month anyway.

faqs.q: How long do CFB Dynasty and CBB Dynasty take, and do they save?
faqs.a: They are the long ones. A single season of recruiting, portal moves and postseason is a proper sit down, and a dynasty is many seasons. Both save your progress in your browser, so you can close the tab mid rebuild and come back to it. The other four games in this section are daily and take a few minutes.

faqs.q: Do I need an account for any of this?
faqs.a: No. Every game on this page plays signed out and free, including both dynasty sims. An account only exists if you want streaks and leaderboard placings to follow you around, and nothing is locked behind it.

problems: FACTS, referenceFacts item 10 and the 'reference' prose. Text: "31 of the 68 NCAA men's basketball tournament spots are automatic bids for conference champions." This is true only of the 2025 and 2026 tournaments, when the Pac-12 lost its automatic bid. It was 32 for years before that, and the NCAA's own expansion release says there will be 32 automatic qualifiers in 2027. The rebuilt Pac-12 launched on July 1, 2026 with nine members and gets its automatic bid back. Stated flat as a standing fact, this is wrong going forward.

FACTS, referenceFacts item 9 and the 'reference' prose. Text: "The NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament has had 68 teams since 2011." Correct through the 2026 tournament, but on May 7, 2026 the NCAA approved expansion to 76 teams beginning with the 2027 tournament. Written in the present perfect on a page that ships as a frozen snapshot, this reads as an ongoing state and becomes false in March 2027, which is roughly six months out.

FACTS, 'reference'. Text: "Basketball's bracket has been steadier, 68 teams since 2011, with 31 of those spots going to conference champions." Carries both errors above, and 'steadier' is now the wrong framing given the field grows by eight teams next season. This is the one sentence in the section that a college hoops reader would catch immediately.

FACTS, staleness. Text: "in 2024 the Pac-12 lost ten members to the Big Ten, Big 12 and ACC, leaving Oregon State and Washington State." Every number is right for 2024, but it is the last thing the paragraph says about the Pac-12, so it reads as the current state. The Pac-12 relaunched on July 1, 2026 with nine full members (Oregon State, Washington State, Boise State, Colorado State, Fresno State, San Diego State, Utah State, Gonzaga, Texas State). A section built on 'the map moved' should not stop two years short.

GAME CLAIMS, startHere /guess-the-college 'why'. Text: "region, conference, mascot and athletic history, which makes it the one to pick if you know campuses and nicknames better than you know any single sport." Guess The College has no mascot clue. Its eleven clues, in src/hooks/useGuessTheCollege.ts lines 13 to 26, are vibe word, region, school size, acceptance rate, conference, basketball history, CFB history, Olympic athletes, NFL draft history, famous alumni, school colors. The mascot clue belongs to the other game: src/pages/GuessCbbTeam.tsx line 21 lists 'region, conference, mascot, tournament success'. The draft has the two clue sets crossed, and the whole 'pick this one if you know nicknames' rationale rests on the wrong half.

GAME CLAIMS, whyHere. Text: "both drip clues out one at a time, region then conference then mascot then postseason history". The drip-feed is real and the score does fall as clues reveal, but the stated order is wrong for Guess The College on three counts: it opens with a vibe word, then region, then school size and acceptance rate, and only reaches conference at clue five.
